facts: Australia is the only country that covers an entire continent, and the sixth largest in the world.
Around 85% of Australians live within 50 kilometres of the coast, leaving the interior almost empty.
The Great Barrier Reef is the largest living structure on Earth and is visible from orbit.
Fiji is made up of over 330 islands, roughly a third of them inhabited.
The 180th meridian passes through the country, so it straddles the theoretical line between hemispheres.
Rugby sevens is the national sport, and Fiji won Olympic gold in it in 2016.
Kiribati straddles the equator and all four hemispheres, spanning some 3.5 million square kilometres of ocean.
It was the first country to enter the year 2000, having shifted the date line east in 1995.
Most of its land sits barely two metres above sea level, making it acutely exposed to rising seas.
The Marshall Islands consists of 29 coral atolls and five isolated islands.
Bikini Atoll was the site of 23 nuclear tests between 1946 and 1958 and remains largely uninhabited.
Traditional Marshallese stick charts mapped ocean swells for navigation between atolls.
The Federated States of Micronesia spans over 600 islands across 2,700 kilometres of the Pacific.
Nan Madol, built on artificial islets of basalt, is the only ancient city constructed atop a coral reef.
The country is a federation of four states, each with its own distinct language and culture.
Nauru is the smallest island country in the world at 21 square kilometres.
It has no official capital city; government offices sit in the Yaren district.
Phosphate mining made it briefly one of the richest countries per person, then left much of the interior stripped.
New Zealand was among the last large landmasses settled by humans, reached by Polynesians around 1300.
It was the first country to grant women the vote in national elections, in 1893.
Wellington is the southernmost capital city of any sovereign state.
Palau created the world's first shark sanctuary in 2009, banning commercial shark fishing in its waters.
Jellyfish Lake holds millions of jellyfish that lost most of their sting through isolation.
Ngerulmud is the least populous capital city of any sovereign state.
Papua New Guinea has over 800 living languages, more than any other country on Earth.
It occupies the eastern half of New Guinea, the world's second largest island.
Much of the highland interior was unknown to outsiders until aerial survey in the 1930s.
Samoa switched to the western side of the international date line in 2011 to align with Australia and New Zealand.
It was the first Pacific island nation to gain independence in the modern era, in 1962.
Traditional tatau tattooing has been practised here continuously for around two thousand years.
The Solomon Islands comprises nearly 1,000 islands spread across the southwestern Pacific.
Guadalcanal was the site of a decisive campaign of the Pacific war in 1942 and 1943.
A high share of the population has naturally blond hair, caused by a gene variant found almost nowhere else.
Tonga is the only Pacific island nation never formally colonised, retaining its monarchy throughout.
It sits beside the Tonga Trench, one of the deepest points in the ocean.
The 2022 Hunga Tonga eruption was among the most powerful recorded and was heard thousands of kilometres away.
Tuvalu is the fourth smallest country in the world at 26 square kilometres.
Its highest point is under five metres, leaving it among the most threatened by sea level rise.
Licensing its .tv internet domain provides a significant share of government revenue.
Vanuatu is an archipelago of about 80 islands formed along a volcanic arc.
It regularly ranks as one of the most natural-disaster-exposed countries in the world.
Land diving on Pentecost Island, where men jump from towers with vines tied to their ankles, inspired bungee jumping.
